physical_harm: Nine injuries, including pellet wounds on the head, neck, chest, arm, and thigh
number_of_offences: Multiple offences charged, but conviction upheld under s. 307 IPC and other provisions
premeditation_planning: The court found the appellant had the knowledge that the act would cause death
key_evidence_accepted: The doctor conducting the post-mortem examination found no internal injuries and opined that the gun was fired from a distant range. He also opined that the death was caused by shock, but did not state that it was due to injuries caused by the appellant or that the deceased profusely bled which could have caused shock.
witness_credibility: The court noted that the prosecution's case was that the deceased died of shock, but there was no evidence to show that the shock was caused by the injuries inflicted by the appellant. The court also mentioned that the prosecution did not bring any evidence to show that the deceased suffered any grievous hurt.

trial_duration.trial_judgment: Judgment and order dated 24th of February, 2000
trial_duration.high_court_decision: Judgment and order dated 9th of February, 2007

legal_representation.accused: Basant R., Shekhar G. Devasa, Karthik Ashok (for Adarsh Upadhyay), Vijay Kumar

investigation_status: Case registered at Bellur Police Station, post-mortem conducted by Dr. Gunashekar V.C.

appeal_history.trial_court: Acquitted both accused of all charges
appeal_history.high_court: Reversed acquittal, convicted under Sections 302, 427 IPC and 27 of the Arms Act
appeal_history.supreme_court: Partially allowed, altered conviction from Section 302 to 307 IPC, sentenced to 10 years rigorous imprisonment

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that there was a long-standing enmity between the families over land, and that the appellant shot at the deceased with the intention to kill him or at least had knowledge that the act would cause death. They also contended that the deceased died within a few hours of the incident, implying that the shock was caused by the gunshot injury.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to prove that the injuries caused by the appellant led to the deceased's death. They emphasized that the doctor's report indicated no internal injuries and that the cause of death was shock, which could have been due to mishandling during transport to the hospital rather than the injuries inflicted by the appellant.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that for an offence under Section 302 IPC (murder), the prosecution must prove that the act of the accused caused the death. If the cause of death is not established, the conviction under Section 302 cannot be sustained. However, if the accused had the intention to kill or knowledge that the act would cause death, the offence under Section 307 IPC (attempt to murder) would apply.
precedent_relied_upon: Bhupendra Singh v. State of UP. 1991 (1) SCR 856
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence of rigorous imprisonment for ten years was imposed because the allegations proved constituted an offence under Section 307 IPC, as the appellant shot at the deceased with the intention to kill or at least had knowledge that the act would cause death.
other_sentence_order: The appellant was also sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for one week for the offence under Section 427, IPC, and his conviction under other penal provisions was maintained. The sentences were directed to run concurrently. The court also directed that the appellant be set at liberty forthwith unless required in any other case.
